title: OFX Rebrand: OzForex Global Brand Standards
subtitle: A brand identity study and 36-page standards guide for OFX
context: Designing Brand Identity, USC Iovine and Young Academy, Fall 2024
role: Brand strategy and personas, lettermark sketches, logo construction, colour and type system, stationery, app and web screens, application mockups, and the 36-page guideline
summary: In 2024 I worked on a brand identity study for OFX, an online foreign-exchange and money-transfer platform, and compiled the system into a 36-page OzForex Global Brand Standards guide. It is an independent identity study I set myself, not commissioned by or made with OFX. Working from written strategy and pencil lettermarks through to a blue isometric cube, I carried the identity across stationery, screens, vehicles and street signage.

sections.heading: Writing before drawing
sections.body:
The early work stayed entirely in words. I defined the company goal around fast, secure and convenient cross-border transfers and anchored the direction to six adjectives, Innovative, Transparent, Reliable, Simple, Global and Inclusive.

Two personas grounded those abstractions in specific transfers. Sophia Huang, a 28-year-old software engineer in Sydney, sends money home to her family. Michael Rivera, a 42-year-old business owner in New York, pays suppliers in Europe. In the finished standards guide, that framing opens with the mission line "Bridging currencies, connecting lives." and ten design tenets.

sections.heading: One-inch squares to a cube
sections.body:
Drawing began with pages of small pencil lettermarks, each confined to a one-inch square to force clear silhouettes. From those grids I pulled three candidates into marker and vector refinement, testing a block-letter OFX, a thin-line OFX, and a cube carrying letters across its faces.

The cube held together best across scales. Building it in Illustrator, I tested four multi-colour palettes ranging from royal blue to navy with sky blue and paired purples before stripping the mark back to a single blue.

sections.heading: Grid, colour and type
sections.body:
The final mark sets O, F and X onto the three visible faces of an isometric cube beside the OzForex wordmark and tagline. Visually it moves away from the existing orange lettering toward a structured blue system built on Pantone 7686 C (#2C439C) and dark grey text (#363639). The guide fixes lockup spacing, a clear zone of at least 50% of the logomark width, and blue, dark and white versions for varying grounds.

For typography I chose Bai Jamjuree from ExtraLight to SemiBold with italic, restricted strictly to lining figures so exchange rates and amounts stay aligned. It reads cleanly across sizes and is freely available through Google Fonts.

sections.heading: Paper, app and web
sections.body:
On paper, the stationery suite covers a letterhead, a blue-flap envelope and a two-sided business card that crops the cube large across one face and places the full lockup on a blue band on the reverse.

In digital screens, the mobile app opens with a white cube on blue before moving into a live rate chart with send and receive figures and a cards view. On the web, the landing page pairs "Bridging currencies, connecting lives" with a transfer calculator, followed by secondary layouts shown on laptops.

sections.heading: Signage, vehicles and a kiosk
sections.body: The closing pages test how the cube holds up in physical space across reception signage, a delivery truck livery, backlit street displays and merchandise. For an unconventional advertising piece, I proposed a currency vending machine for airports, universities and trade shows that displays live exchange rates and dispenses coupons or app credits for foreign currency.
